reasoning: The stem pairs an active 11:00 discharge order with unresolved physiologic and psychosocial barriers documented at 09:15: desaturation to 89% after 40 feet requiring oxygen to recover, failed teach-back on new medications and warning signs, inability to afford the prescribed diuretic, no home scale, and living alone in a second-floor walk-up. C2 (unsafe premature discharge) is the only condition token that names this discrepancy. C1 is contradicted because the failed teach-back and unmet resource needs make standard written instructions insufficient. C3 is contradicted because BNP and weight are improving, so the client is not in continued acute decompensation requiring indefinite inpatient treatment. Among actions, A3 addresses the time-critical physiologic finding by advocating to hold the discharge with objective safety data and escalating as needed, and A1 addresses the affordability, home-scale, isolation, and education barriers through case management, social work, clinical pharmacy, and home-health planning. A2 is contradicted by the same safety findings, and A4 repeats the education modality that already failed and leaves the oxygenation and resource barriers unaddressed. Among parameters, P2 directly re-evaluates the exertional desaturation and the stair demand created by the second-floor walk-up, and P1 directly re-evaluates the failed teach-back on medications, daily weights, call parameters, and warning signs. P3 and P4 are already improving in the stem and, restricted to a single inpatient measure, do not evaluate either identified barrier or the client's readiness for the home environment.
